newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico net assets rise to Nov 8.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico net assets rise to Nov 8.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said Tuesday its net international assets as of November 8, 1996, were $4.411 billion, compared with $4.378 billion on November 1.
The central bank said that its net international reserves as of November 8 were $15.897 billion, compared with $16.122 billion as of November 1.
It said the increase of $33 million in international assets in the week was due to:
- Net revenues from operations with state oil firm Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) of $373 million
- Net sales of foreign currency to the federal government worth $154 million, mainly for foreign debt service payments
- Interest payments to the International Monetary Fund worth $154 million

- A net loss of $32 million for a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts of commercial banks at the central bank.
Banco de Mexico said the monetary base fell by 1.602 billion pesos due to revesal of the seasonal demand for notes and coins seen in the previous week.
The balance of the government's deposits with the central bank fell by 10.405 billion pesos, mainly as a result of transfers of funds to states, payments to teachers and external debt service.
Central bank credit to banks fell by 11.349 billion pesos to compensate for the monetary impact of the transfer of funds from the federal treasury and the lower demand for notes and coins.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's assets and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six month duration from other central banks.
